Explorables from courses and tutorials. Everything here runs in your browser;
nothing to install. Change a slider while a simulation is running and it reacts
immediately.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
// shared helpers: one persistent canvas per explorable, text-sized fonts, responsive width
exFont = "16px " + getComputedStyle(document.body).fontFamily
exFg = () => getComputedStyle(document.body).color
mkCanvas = (W, H) => {
  const c = DOM.context2d(W, H);
  c.canvas.style.width = "100%"; c.canvas.style.maxWidth = W + "px"; c.canvas.style.height = "auto";
  return c;
}
axisBox = (c, x, y, w, h) => { c.strokeStyle = "#999"; c.lineWidth = 1; c.strokeRect(x, y, w, h); }
```

## A leaky integrate-and-fire neuron

The neuron's membrane potential $V$ integrates its input current $I$ and leaks
back towards rest. Whenever $V$ reaches the threshold $V_{\text{th}}$, a spike
is emitted and $V$ is reset.

$$\tau_m \frac{dV}{dt} = (V_{\text{rest}} - V) + R\,I(t)$$

- $V$: membrane potential in mV. $V_{\text{rest}} = -65$ mV is the resting
  potential it leaks back to; after a spike it is reset to $V_{\text{reset}} = -70$ mV
  and held there for a refractory period of 2 ms.
- $I(t)$: input current in nA. With noise switched on, a random Gaussian
  fluctuation is added at every time step; the slider sets its strength.
- $\tau_m$: membrane time constant in ms, how quickly $V$ follows a change in input.
- $R = 2$ MΩ: input resistance, fixed. $V_{\text{th}}$: the threshold slider.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof lifI = Inputs.range([0, 25], {value: 8, step: 0.5, label: "Input current (nA)"})
viewof lifNoise = Inputs.range([0, 10], {value: 0, step: 0.5, label: "Input noise (0 = off)"})
viewof lifTau = Inputs.range([2, 50], {value: 10, step: 1, label: "Membrane time constant τ (ms)"})
viewof lifThr = Inputs.range([-60, -35], {value: -50, step: 1, label: "Threshold (mV)"})
viewof lifPause = Inputs.toggle({label: "Pause"})
viewof lifReset = Inputs.button("Reset (also clears the f-I points)")
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
lifState = {
  lifReset;
  const dt = 0.1, win = 300, R = 2, Vrest = -65, Vreset = -70, refr = 2;
  const n = Math.round(win / dt);
  const V = new Float32Array(n).fill(Vrest), Iarr = new Float32Array(n);
  let v = Vrest, refrLeft = 0, t = 0;
  const fi = new Map();
  let key = null, sinceChange = 0, spikesSince = 0, lastSig = 0;
  const gauss = () => { let u = 0; while (u === 0) u = Math.random();
                        return Math.sqrt(-2 * Math.log(u)) * Math.cos(2 * Math.PI * Math.random()); };
  while (true) {
    const I0 = viewof lifI.value, sig = viewof lifNoise.value,
          tau = viewof lifTau.value, thr = viewof lifThr.value;
    if (!viewof lifPause.value) {
      const k = `${I0}|${sig > 0}`;
      if (sig > 0 && sig !== lastSig) { for (const [kk, p] of fi) if (p.noisy) fi.delete(kk); }
      if (sig > 0) lastSig = sig;
      if (k !== key) { key = k; sinceChange = 0; spikesSince = 0; }
      for (let s = 0; s < 20; s++) {
        const I = I0 + sig * gauss() / Math.sqrt(dt);
        if (refrLeft > 0) { refrLeft -= dt; v = Vreset; }
        else {
          v += dt / tau * ((Vrest - v) + R * I);
          if (v >= thr) { v = 20; spikesSince++; refrLeft = refr; }
        }
        V.copyWithin(0, 1); V[n - 1] = v;
        Iarr.copyWithin(0, 1); Iarr[n - 1] = I;
        if (v === 20) v = Vreset;
        t += dt; sinceChange += dt;
      }
      if (sinceChange >= 500) fi.set(key, {I: I0, noisy: sig > 0, rate: 1000 * spikesSince / sinceChange});
    }
    yield {V, Iarr, t, win, fi, thr, tau, sig, I0, R, Vrest, refr,
           rate: sinceChange > 0 ? 1000 * spikesSince / sinceChange : 0};
  }
}
lifCanvas = mkCanvas(760, 360)
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
{
  const {V, Iarr, win, fi, thr, tau, sig, I0, R, Vrest, refr, rate} = lifState;
  const blue = "#1f77b4", orange = "#ff7f0e", c = lifCanvas, fg = exFg();
  const W = 760, H = 360, n = V.length;
  c.clearRect(0, 0, W, H); c.font = exFont;
  // traces, left
  const mL = 80, trR = 470;
  const top = {y0: 12, h: 80, lo: -10, hi: 35};
  const bot = {y0: 112, h: 200, lo: -80, hi: 30};
  const sx = i => mL + (trR - mL) * i / (n - 1);
  const sy = (p, v) => p.y0 + p.h * (1 - (v - p.lo) / (p.hi - p.lo));
  for (const p of [top, bot]) axisBox(c, mL, p.y0, trR - mL, p.h);
  c.fillStyle = fg; c.textAlign = "right";
  c.fillText("I (nA)", mL - 8, top.y0 + top.h / 2 + 5);
  c.fillText("V (mV)", mL - 8, bot.y0 + bot.h / 2 + 5);
  c.fillText(thr, mL - 8, sy(bot, thr) + 5); c.fillText("-65", mL - 8, sy(bot, -65) + 5);
  c.textAlign = "center"; c.fillText(`last ${win} ms`, (mL + trR) / 2, H - 14);
  c.textAlign = "right"; c.fillText(`${rate.toFixed(0)} spikes / s`, trR - 8, bot.y0 + 20);
  c.setLineDash([4, 4]); c.strokeStyle = "red"; c.beginPath(); c.moveTo(mL, sy(bot, thr)); c.lineTo(trR, sy(bot, thr)); c.stroke(); c.setLineDash([]);
  c.strokeStyle = "#888"; c.lineWidth = 1; c.beginPath();
  for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) { const y = sy(top, Math.max(top.lo, Math.min(top.hi, Iarr[i]))); i ? c.lineTo(sx(i), y) : c.moveTo(sx(0), y); }
  c.stroke();
  c.strokeStyle = sig > 0 ? orange : blue; c.lineWidth = 1.5; c.beginPath();
  for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) i ? c.lineTo(sx(i), sy(bot, V[i])) : c.moveTo(sx(0), sy(bot, V[0]));
  c.stroke();
  // f-I curve, right
  const fP = {x0: 560, y0: 12, w: 180, h: 300};
  const Imax = 25, fmax = Math.max(100, ...Array.from(fi.values()).map(p => p.rate)) * 1.1;
  const fx = I => fP.x0 + fP.w * I / Imax, fy = f => fP.y0 + fP.h * (1 - f / fmax);
  axisBox(c, fP.x0, fP.y0, fP.w, fP.h);
  c.fillStyle = fg; c.textAlign = "center";
  c.fillText("input (nA)", fP.x0 + fP.w / 2, H - 14);
  c.fillText("0", fx(0), fP.y0 + fP.h + 20); c.fillText(Imax, fx(Imax), fP.y0 + fP.h + 20);
  c.save(); c.translate(fP.x0 - 44, fP.y0 + fP.h / 2); c.rotate(-Math.PI / 2); c.fillText("spikes / s", 0, 0); c.restore();
  c.textAlign = "right"; c.fillText("0", fP.x0 - 6, fy(0) + 5); c.fillText(fmax.toFixed(0), fP.x0 - 6, fy(fmax) + 5);
  c.setLineDash([3, 3]); c.strokeStyle = blue; c.lineWidth = 1; c.beginPath(); let started = false;
  for (let I = 0; I <= Imax; I += 0.1) {
    const d = R * I - (thr - Vrest); if (d <= 0) continue;
    const f = Math.min(fmax, 1000 / (refr + tau * Math.log(R * I / d)));
    started ? c.lineTo(fx(I), fy(f)) : c.moveTo(fx(I), fy(f)); started = true;
  }
  c.stroke(); c.setLineDash([]);
  for (const [k, p] of fi) { c.fillStyle = p.noisy ? orange : blue; c.beginPath(); c.arc(fx(p.I), fy(p.rate), 5, 0, 2 * Math.PI); c.fill(); }
  c.strokeStyle = sig > 0 ? orange : blue; c.lineWidth = 2; c.beginPath(); c.arc(fx(I0), fy(Math.min(rate, fmax)), 8, 0, 2 * Math.PI); c.stroke();
  c.textAlign = "left"; c.fillStyle = blue; c.fillText("noise-free", fP.x0 + 8, fP.y0 + 22);
  c.fillStyle = orange; c.fillText(sig > 0 ? `noise ${sig}` : "noise (off)", fP.x0 + 8, fP.y0 + 44);
  return c.canvas;
}
```

**What you see.** Left, top: the input current $I$ in grey, over the last 300 ms.
Left, bottom: the membrane potential $V$, blue when the input is noise-free,
orange when noise is on. The red dashed line is the threshold; the spikes are
drawn as vertical strokes up to +20 mV. The number in the corner is the current
firing rate.

Right: the **f-I curve**, firing rate against input current. Every input
strength you try adds a dot once the neuron has run for half a second at that
setting; blue dots are noise-free measurements, orange dots are measurements at
the current noise level (changing the noise level clears them). The open ring
marks the setting you are looking at now. The blue dashed line is the exact rate
of the noise-free neuron, $f = 1 / \left(t_{\text{ref}} + \tau_m \ln \frac{RI}{RI - (V_{\text{th}} - V_{\text{rest}})}\right)$,
which is zero below $I = (V_{\text{th}} - V_{\text{rest}})/R$. Noise lets the
neuron fire below that point and rounds off the curve.

Try: increase the current until the neuron starts to fire, then add noise at a
sub-threshold current. From the webinar for the German Neuroscience Olympiad 2020.
[Notebook on GitHub](https://github.com/SigridTraegenap/DNO_webinar_2020) ·
[Open in Google Colab](https://colab.research.google.com/github/SigridTraegenap/DNO_webinar_2020/blob/master/Leaky%20Integrate%20and%20Fire%20neuron%20model.ipynb)

## Principal component analysis

Fisher's iris data: 150 flowers, four measurements each. PCA finds the
directions of largest variance, the eigenvectors of the covariance matrix.

$$C = \frac{1}{n} X^{\mathsf T} X, \qquad C\, e_k = \lambda_k e_k$$

- $X$: the data matrix, 150 rows (flowers) and 4 columns (sepal length, sepal
  width, petal length, petal width, in cm), with the column means removed.
  With standardisation on, each column is also divided by its standard deviation.
- $C$: the $4 \times 4$ covariance matrix.
- $e_k$: the $k$-th principal component, a direction in the four-dimensional
  measurement space; $\lambda_k$ its eigenvalue, the variance of the data along it.
- Explained variance: $\lambda_k / \sum_j \lambda_j$.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
irisRaw = FileAttachment("assets/iris.json").json()
viewof pcStd = Inputs.toggle({label: "Standardise each variable (z-score)", value: true})
pcAxisOpts = new Map([["PC 1", "pc0"], ["PC 2", "pc1"], ["PC 3", "pc2"], ["PC 4", "pc3"],
  ...irisRaw.features.map((f, i) => [f, "v" + i])])
viewof pcX = Inputs.select(pcAxisOpts, {value: "pc0", label: "Horizontal axis"})
viewof pcY = Inputs.select(pcAxisOpts, {value: "pc1", label: "Vertical axis"})
viewof pcColour = Inputs.toggle({label: "Colour by species", value: true})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
symEig = A => {           // Jacobi eigenvalue iteration for a small symmetric matrix
  const n = A.length, a = A.map(r => r.slice()), v = Array.from({length: n}, (_, i) => Array.from({length: n}, (_, j) => +(i === j)));
  for (let sweep = 0; sweep < 60; sweep++) {
    let off = 0; for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) for (let j = i + 1; j < n; j++) off += a[i][j] ** 2;
    if (off < 1e-18) break;
    for (let p = 0; p < n; p++) for (let q = p + 1; q < n; q++) {
      if (Math.abs(a[p][q]) < 1e-15) continue;
      const th = (a[q][q] - a[p][p]) / (2 * a[p][q]), t = Math.sign(th || 1) / (Math.abs(th) + Math.sqrt(th * th + 1));
      const cs = 1 / Math.sqrt(t * t + 1), sn = t * cs;
      for (let k = 0; k < n; k++) { const akp = a[k][p], akq = a[k][q]; a[k][p] = cs * akp - sn * akq; a[k][q] = sn * akp + cs * akq; }
      for (let k = 0; k < n; k++) { const apk = a[p][k], aqk = a[q][k]; a[p][k] = cs * apk - sn * aqk; a[q][k] = sn * apk + cs * aqk; }
      for (let k = 0; k < n; k++) { const vkp = v[k][p], vkq = v[k][q]; v[k][p] = cs * vkp - sn * vkq; v[k][q] = sn * vkp + cs * vkq; }
    }
  }
  const order = [...Array(n).keys()].sort((i, j) => a[j][j] - a[i][i]);
  return {values: order.map(i => a[i][i]), vectors: order.map(i => { const col = v.map(r => r[i]); const big = col.reduce((b, x) => Math.abs(x) > Math.abs(b) ? x : b, 0); return big < 0 ? col.map(x => -x) : col; })};
}
pca = {
  const rows = irisRaw.rows, d = 4, n = rows.length;
  const mean = Array.from({length: d}, (_, j) => rows.reduce((s, r) => s + r[j], 0) / n);
  const sd = Array.from({length: d}, (_, j) => Math.sqrt(rows.reduce((s, r) => s + (r[j] - mean[j]) ** 2, 0) / n));
  const X = rows.map(r => Array.from({length: d}, (_, j) => (r[j] - mean[j]) / (pcStd ? sd[j] : 1)));
  const C = Array.from({length: d}, (_, i) => Array.from({length: d}, (_, j) => X.reduce((s, x) => s + x[i] * x[j], 0) / n));
  const {values, vectors} = symEig(C);
  const scores = X.map(x => vectors.map(e => e.reduce((s, ei, j) => s + ei * x[j], 0)));
  const total = values.reduce((s, l) => s + l, 0);
  return {X, C, values, vectors, scores, total, species: rows.map(r => r[4]), mean, sd};
}
pcCanvas = mkCanvas(760, 580)
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
{
  const c = pcCanvas, fg = exFg(), W = 760, H = 580, cols = ["#1f77b4", "#ff7f0e", "#2ca02c"];
  const {X, values, vectors, scores, total, species} = pca, feats = irisRaw.features;
  c.clearRect(0, 0, W, H); c.font = exFont;
  const get = (key, i) => key.startsWith("pc") ? scores[i][+key[2]] : X[i][+key[1]];
  const label = key => key.startsWith("pc") ? `PC ${+key[2] + 1}` : feats[+key[1]] + (pcStd ? " (z-scored)" : " (cm, centred)");
  const xs = X.map((_, i) => get(pcX, i)), ys = X.map((_, i) => get(pcY, i));
  const lim = Math.max(...xs.map(Math.abs), ...ys.map(Math.abs)) * 1.1;
  const sP = {x0: 90, y0: 12, s: 360};
  const px = v => sP.x0 + sP.s * (v + lim) / (2 * lim), py = v => sP.y0 + sP.s * (1 - (v + lim) / (2 * lim));
  axisBox(c, sP.x0, sP.y0, sP.s, sP.s);
  c.strokeStyle = "#ccc"; c.lineWidth = 1; c.beginPath(); c.moveTo(px(0), sP.y0); c.lineTo(px(0), sP.y0 + sP.s); c.moveTo(sP.x0, py(0)); c.lineTo(sP.x0 + sP.s, py(0)); c.stroke();
  // principal axes drawn in the plane of two raw variables
  if (!pcX.startsWith("pc") && !pcY.startsWith("pc")) {
    const i = +pcX[1], j = +pcY[1];
    for (const [k, col] of [[0, "#d62728"], [1, "#9467bd"]]) {
      const e = vectors[k], L = 2 * Math.sqrt(values[k]);
      c.strokeStyle = col; c.lineWidth = 3; c.beginPath(); c.moveTo(px(-L * e[i]), py(-L * e[j])); c.lineTo(px(L * e[i]), py(L * e[j])); c.stroke();
      c.fillStyle = col; c.textAlign = "left"; c.fillText(`PC ${k + 1}`, px(L * e[i]) + 6, py(L * e[j]) + 5);
    }
  }
  X.forEach((_, i) => { c.fillStyle = pcColour ? cols[species[i]] : "#555"; c.globalAlpha = 0.6; c.beginPath(); c.arc(px(xs[i]), py(ys[i]), 4.5, 0, 2 * Math.PI); c.fill(); });
  c.globalAlpha = 1; c.fillStyle = fg; c.textAlign = "center";
  c.fillText(label(pcX), sP.x0 + sP.s / 2, sP.y0 + sP.s + 24);
  c.fillText((-lim).toFixed(1), sP.x0, sP.y0 + sP.s + 44); c.fillText(lim.toFixed(1), sP.x0 + sP.s, sP.y0 + sP.s + 44);
  c.save(); c.translate(sP.x0 - 60, sP.y0 + sP.s / 2); c.rotate(-Math.PI / 2); c.fillText(label(pcY), 0, 0); c.restore();
  c.textAlign = "right"; c.fillText(lim.toFixed(1), sP.x0 - 8, sP.y0 + 6); c.fillText((-lim).toFixed(1), sP.x0 - 8, sP.y0 + sP.s + 2);
  if (pcColour) irisRaw.species.forEach((s, k) => { c.fillStyle = cols[k]; c.textAlign = "left"; c.fillText(s, sP.x0 + 10, sP.y0 + 22 + 22 * k); });
  // explained variance bars, right
  const bP = {x0: 520, y0: 12, w: 220, h: 150};
  axisBox(c, bP.x0, bP.y0, bP.w, bP.h);
  values.forEach((l, k) => {
    const frac = l / total, bw = bP.w / 4 * 0.7, bx = bP.x0 + bP.w * (k + 0.15) / 4;
    c.fillStyle = "#1f77b4"; c.fillRect(bx, bP.y0 + bP.h * (1 - frac), bw, bP.h * frac);
    c.fillStyle = fg; c.textAlign = "center"; c.fillText(`${(100 * frac).toFixed(0)}%`, bx + bw / 2, bP.y0 + bP.h * (1 - frac) - 6);
    c.fillText(`PC ${k + 1}`, bx + bw / 2, bP.y0 + bP.h + 22);
  });
  c.fillStyle = fg; c.textAlign = "center"; c.fillText("explained variance", bP.x0 + bP.w / 2, bP.y0 + bP.h + 44);
  // loadings table, full width below the scatter
  const tY = 470, colX = j => 250 + 125 * j;
  c.fillStyle = fg; c.textAlign = "left"; c.fillText("loadings: components of each eₖ", 90, tY);
  c.font = "14px " + getComputedStyle(document.body).fontFamily;
  feats.forEach((f, j) => { c.textAlign = "center"; c.fillText(f, colX(j), tY + 24); });
  values.forEach((_, k) => {
    c.textAlign = "left"; c.fillText(`PC ${k + 1}`, 90, tY + 46 + 20 * k);
    vectors[k].forEach((e, j) => { c.textAlign = "center"; c.fillText(e.toFixed(2), colX(j), tY + 46 + 20 * k); });
  });
  return c.canvas;
}
```

**What you see.** Left: each flower as a dot in the chosen coordinates. With
species colouring on, blue is *setosa*, orange *versicolor*, green *virginica*;
off, every dot is grey, which is what PCA itself sees, since it never uses the
labels. When both axes are raw measurements, the first two principal components
are drawn as lines through the origin, PC 1 in red and PC 2 in purple, each
scaled to two standard deviations of the data along it. Right, top: the share of
the total variance carried by each component, as blue bars. Right, bottom: the
loadings, how much of each measurement goes into each component.

Try: switch standardisation off and PC 1 is dominated by petal length, simply
because it has the largest spread in centimetres. Look at the raw-variable
planes to see where PC 1 points. From the dimensionality-reduction exercise in
*Theoretical Neuroscience*.

## Sampling and the discrete Fourier transform

A signal made of two sine waves is sampled at $N$ points spaced $\Delta x$
apart over an interval of length $T$. The discrete Fourier transform (DFT)
decomposes the samples into frequencies $f_m = m / T$:

$$y(x) = a_1 \sin(2\pi f_1 x) + a_2 \sin(2\pi f_2 x), \qquad
Y_m = \sum_{n=0}^{N-1} y_n\, e^{-2\pi i\, m n / N}$$

- $f_1, f_2$: frequencies of the two components in cycles per unit length; $a_1, a_2$ their amplitudes.
- $\Delta x$: sampling interval. $T$: interval length, so $N = T / \Delta x$.
- $|Y_m| \cdot 2/N$: the amplitude the DFT assigns to frequency $f_m = m/T$.
- Nyquist frequency $f_{\text{Ny}} = 1 / (2 \Delta x)$: the highest frequency the
  samples can represent. Anything above it is *aliased* to a lower frequency.
- $K$: how many of the strongest DFT components are used to rebuild the signal.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof ftF1 = Inputs.range([0, 12], {value: 1, step: 0.1, label: "f₁ (cycles / unit)"})
viewof ftA1 = Inputs.range([0, 2], {value: 1, step: 0.1, label: "a₁"})
viewof ftF2 = Inputs.range([0, 12], {value: 3.5, step: 0.1, label: "f₂ (cycles / unit)"})
viewof ftA2 = Inputs.range([0, 2], {value: 0.5, step: 0.1, label: "a₂"})
viewof ftDx = Inputs.range([0.02, 0.5], {value: 0.1, step: 0.01, label: "Sampling interval Δx"})
viewof ftT = Inputs.range([1, 8], {value: 4, step: 0.5, label: "Interval length T"})
viewof ftK = Inputs.range([0, 10], {value: 2, step: 1, label: "K components kept for reconstruction"})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
ft = {
  const T = ftT, dx = ftDx, N = Math.max(4, Math.floor(T / dx)), x0 = -T / 2;
  const sig = x => ftA1 * Math.sin(2 * Math.PI * ftF1 * x) + ftA2 * Math.sin(2 * Math.PI * ftF2 * x);
  const xs = Array.from({length: N}, (_, n) => x0 + n * dx), ys = xs.map(sig);
  const M = Math.floor(N / 2), re = new Float64Array(M + 1), im = new Float64Array(M + 1);
  for (let m = 0; m <= M; m++) for (let n = 0; n < N; n++) { const a = -2 * Math.PI * m * n / N; re[m] += ys[n] * Math.cos(a); im[m] += ys[n] * Math.sin(a); }
  const amp = Array.from({length: M + 1}, (_, m) => ({m, f: m / T, A: (m === 0 ? 1 : 2) * Math.hypot(re[m], im[m]) / N, ph: Math.atan2(im[m], re[m])}));
  const kept = amp.slice(1).sort((a, b) => b.A - a.A).slice(0, ftK);
  const rec = x => amp[0].A * Math.cos(amp[0].ph) + kept.reduce((s, c) => s + c.A * Math.cos(2 * Math.PI * c.f * (x - x0) + c.ph), 0);
  const fine = Array.from({length: 600}, (_, i) => x0 + T * i / 599);
  const fNy = 1 / (2 * dx);
  const alias = f => { const fs = 2 * fNy; let g = Math.abs(f - Math.round(f / fs) * fs); return g; };
  return {T, dx, N, x0, xs, ys, fine, sig, rec, amp, kept, fNy, alias};
}
ftCanvas = mkCanvas(760, 450)
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
{
  const c = ftCanvas, fg = exFg(), W = 760, H = 450, blue = "#1f77b4", orange = "#ff7f0e";
  const {T, N, x0, xs, ys, fine, sig, rec, amp, kept, fNy, alias} = ft;
  c.clearRect(0, 0, W, H); c.font = exFont;
  // signal panel
  const sP = {x0: 80, y0: 12, w: W - 100, h: 170};
  const ymax = Math.max(0.5, ftA1 + ftA2) * 1.15;
  const sx = x => sP.x0 + sP.w * (x - x0) / T, sy = y => sP.y0 + sP.h * (1 - (y + ymax) / (2 * ymax));
  axisBox(c, sP.x0, sP.y0, sP.w, sP.h);
  c.strokeStyle = "#888"; c.lineWidth = 1; c.beginPath(); c.moveTo(sP.x0, sy(0)); c.lineTo(sP.x0 + sP.w, sy(0)); c.stroke();
  c.strokeStyle = "#aaa"; c.lineWidth = 1.5; c.beginPath(); fine.forEach((x, i) => i ? c.lineTo(sx(x), sy(sig(x))) : c.moveTo(sx(x), sy(sig(x)))); c.stroke();
  c.strokeStyle = orange; c.lineWidth = 2; c.beginPath(); fine.forEach((x, i) => i ? c.lineTo(sx(x), sy(rec(x))) : c.moveTo(sx(x), sy(rec(x)))); c.stroke();
  c.fillStyle = blue; xs.forEach((x, n) => { c.beginPath(); c.arc(sx(x), sy(ys[n]), 3.5, 0, 2 * Math.PI); c.fill(); });
  c.fillStyle = fg; c.textAlign = "center"; c.fillText(`x  ·  N = ${N} samples`, sP.x0 + sP.w / 2, sP.y0 + sP.h + 22);
  c.textAlign = "right"; c.fillText("y", sP.x0 - 10, sP.y0 + sP.h / 2 + 5);
  c.fillText(ymax.toFixed(1), sP.x0 - 8, sP.y0 + 6); c.fillText((-ymax).toFixed(1), sP.x0 - 8, sP.y0 + sP.h + 2);
  // spectrum panel
  const pP = {x0: 80, y0: 240, w: W - 100, h: 140};
  const fmax = Math.max(fNy * 1.05, 0.5), Amax = Math.max(0.5, ...amp.slice(1).map(a => a.A)) * 1.15;
  const fx = f => pP.x0 + pP.w * f / fmax, fy = A => pP.y0 + pP.h * (1 - A / Amax);
  axisBox(c, pP.x0, pP.y0, pP.w, pP.h);
  c.setLineDash([4, 4]); c.strokeStyle = "red"; c.beginPath(); c.moveTo(fx(fNy), pP.y0); c.lineTo(fx(fNy), pP.y0 + pP.h); c.stroke();
  c.strokeStyle = "#2ca02c";
  for (const [f, a] of [[ftF1, ftA1], [ftF2, ftA2]]) if (a > 0) { const g = alias(f); c.beginPath(); c.moveTo(fx(g), pP.y0); c.lineTo(fx(g), pP.y0 + pP.h); c.stroke(); }
  c.setLineDash([]);
  for (const a of amp.slice(1)) {
    const isKept = kept.includes(a);
    c.strokeStyle = isKept ? orange : blue; c.lineWidth = isKept ? 3 : 1.5;
    c.beginPath(); c.moveTo(fx(a.f), fy(0)); c.lineTo(fx(a.f), fy(a.A)); c.stroke();
    c.fillStyle = isKept ? orange : blue; c.beginPath(); c.arc(fx(a.f), fy(a.A), 3, 0, 2 * Math.PI); c.fill();
  }
  c.fillStyle = fg; c.textAlign = "center";
  c.fillText(`frequency (cycles / unit)  ·  Nyquist ${fNy.toFixed(2)}`, pP.x0 + pP.w / 2, pP.y0 + pP.h + 22);
  c.fillText("0", fx(0), pP.y0 + pP.h + 42); c.fillText(fmax.toFixed(1), fx(fmax), pP.y0 + pP.h + 42);
  c.textAlign = "right"; c.fillText("|Y|·2/N", pP.x0 - 10, pP.y0 + pP.h / 2 + 5);
  c.fillText(Amax.toFixed(1), pP.x0 - 8, pP.y0 + 6); c.fillText("0", pP.x0 - 8, pP.y0 + pP.h + 2);
  return c.canvas;
}
```

**What you see.** Top: the true continuous signal in grey, its samples as blue
dots, and in orange the signal rebuilt from the $K$ strongest DFT components.
Bottom: the amplitude spectrum, one stem per DFT frequency $f_m = m/T$, up to
the Nyquist frequency marked by the red dashed line. Stems used in the
reconstruction are orange, the rest blue. The green dashed lines mark where the
two true frequencies $f_1$ and $f_2$ land in the spectrum; when a frequency
lies above Nyquist, its green line sits at the aliased frequency instead.

Try: set $f_2$ above the Nyquist frequency and watch its energy appear at the
wrong place. Make $T$ a non-integer multiple of the period and the peak smears
over neighbouring frequencies (leakage). With $K = 2$ and well-resolved peaks,
the orange reconstruction sits exactly on the grey signal. From the Fourier
exercises in *Theoretical Neuroscience*.

## Difference of Gaussians and its spectrum

A local-excitation, lateral-inhibition kernel is the difference of two
Gaussians. Its Fourier transform tells you which spatial frequency a recurrent
network with this kernel will amplify most; the next explorable shows that
network in action.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof sigE = Inputs.range([0.1, 10], {value: 1, step: 0.1, label: "Excitation width σₑ"})
viewof ampE = Inputs.range([0, 10], {value: 1, step: 0.1, label: "Excitation strength"})
viewof sigI = Inputs.range([0.1, 10], {value: 2, step: 0.1, label: "Inhibition width σᵢ"})
viewof ampI = Inputs.range([0, 2], {value: 1, step: 0.05, label: "Inhibition strength"})

gauss = (x, s) => Math.exp(-0.5 * x * x / (s * s)) / (Math.sqrt(2 * Math.PI) * s)
ghat = (f, s) => Math.exp(-2 * Math.PI * Math.PI * s * s * f * f)
xmax = 5 * Math.max(sigE, sigI)
space = Array.from({length: 401}, (_, i) => {
  const x = -xmax + 2 * xmax * i / 400;
  const e = ampE * gauss(x, sigE), inh = -ampI * gauss(x, sigI);
  return {x, Excitation: e, Inhibition: inh, "Difference of Gaussians": e + inh};
})
spectrum = Array.from({length: 401}, (_, i) => { const f = 2 * i / 400; return {f, k: Math.abs(ampE * ghat(f, sigE) - ampI * ghat(f, sigI))}; })
peak = spectrum.reduce((a, b) => (b.k > a.k ? b : a))

html`<div style="display:flex;flex-wrap:wrap;gap:1rem">
${Plot.plot({
  width: 370, height: 280, marginLeft: 40, style: {fontSize: "15px"},
  x: {label: "space"}, y: {label: null, ticks: 0},
  color: {legend: true, domain: ["Excitation", "Inhibition", "Difference of Gaussians"], range: ["#ff7f0e", "#1f77b4", "black"]},
  marks: [Plot.ruleY([0], {stroke: "#999"}),
    ...["Excitation", "Inhibition", "Difference of Gaussians"].map(k => Plot.line(space, {x: "x", y: k, stroke: () => k, strokeWidth: 2}))]
})}
${Plot.plot({
  width: 370, height: 280, marginLeft: 50, style: {fontSize: "15px"},
  x: {label: "spatial frequency (cycles / unit length)"},
  y: {label: "|kernel spectrum|", domain: [0, Math.max(0.05, ampE, ampI)]},
  marks: [Plot.line(spectrum, {x: "f", y: "k", stroke: "gray", strokeWidth: 2}),
    Plot.ruleX([peak.f], {stroke: "#ff7f0e", strokeDasharray: "4 4"}),
    Plot.text([peak], {x: "f", y: "k", text: d => `peak at f = ${d.f.toFixed(2)}`, dx: 8, dy: -8, textAnchor: "start"})]
})}
</div>`
```

**What you see.** Left: the excitatory Gaussian in orange, the inhibitory one
in blue (drawn negative), and their difference in black, as functions of
distance. $\sigma_e$ and $\sigma_i$ are the widths; the strength sliders scale
the two curves. Right: the magnitude of the kernel's Fourier transform in grey;
the orange dashed line marks the spatial frequency with the largest value, the
one a recurrent network with this kernel amplifies most.

## Pattern formation in a recurrent network

A ring of neurons, each exciting its close neighbours and inhibiting those a
bit further away. Such a kernel amplifies one spatial frequency more than any
other, so even random input turns into a regular pattern.

$$\tau \frac{dr}{dt} = -r + \left[\,W r + h\,\right]_+$$

- $r$: the firing rates of the 256 neurons on the ring.
- $W$: the connection matrix. Neuron $i$ receives from neuron $j$ a weight that
  depends only on their distance: a narrow positive Gaussian (excitation) minus a
  wider negative one (inhibition). The two width sliders set those Gaussians.
- $h$: a fixed random external input, one value per neuron, plus optional noise
  that is redrawn at every time step (the noise slider).
- $[\cdot]_+$: rectification, negative values are set to zero.
- $\tau$: the time constant; the clock in the figure counts in units of $\tau$.
- Gain: $W$ is scaled so that its largest eigenvalue equals the gain slider.
  Above 1 the corresponding pattern grows; below 1 it decays.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof rnSigE = Inputs.range([1, 25], {value: 5, step: 0.5, label: "Excitation width"})
viewof rnSigI = Inputs.range([1, 50], {value: 12, step: 0.5, label: "Inhibition width"})
viewof rnGain = Inputs.range([0.2, 1.6], {value: 1.2, step: 0.02, label: "Gain (largest eigenvalue of W)"})
viewof rnNoise = Inputs.range([0, 1], {value: 0.1, step: 0.02, label: "Input noise"})
viewof rnPause = Inputs.toggle({label: "Pause"})
viewof rnReset = Inputs.button("Reset")
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
rnN = 256
rnKernel = {
  const N = rnN, sE = rnSigE, sI = rnSigI;
  const g = (d, s) => Math.exp(-0.5 * d * d / (s * s)) / s;
  const k = new Float64Array(N);
  for (let d = 0; d < N; d++) { const dd = Math.min(d, N - d); k[d] = g(dd, sE) - g(dd, sI); }
  const ev = new Float64Array(N / 2 + 1);
  for (let m = 0; m <= N / 2; m++) { let s = 0; for (let d = 0; d < N; d++) s += k[d] * Math.cos(2 * Math.PI * m * d / N); ev[m] = s; }
  let lmax = -Infinity, mmax = 0; for (let m = 0; m <= N / 2; m++) if (ev[m] > lmax) { lmax = ev[m]; mmax = m; }
  const scale = rnGain / lmax;
  return {N, k: k.map(x => x * scale), ev: ev.map(x => x * scale), mmax};
}
rnState = {
  rnReset;
  const N = rnN, dt = 0.1, tau = 1;
  const h = Float64Array.from({length: N}, () => 0.5 + 0.5 * Math.random());
  let r = new Float64Array(N).fill(0.5), t = 0;
  while (true) {
    if (!viewof rnPause.value) {
      const {k} = rnKernel; const noise = viewof rnNoise.value;
      for (let step = 0; step < 5; step++) {
        const rn = new Float64Array(N);
        for (let i = 0; i < N; i++) {
          let s = 0;
          for (let j = 0; j < N; j++) { const d = (i - j + N) % N; s += k[d] * r[j]; }
          rn[i] = r[i] + dt / tau * (-r[i] + Math.max(0, s + h[i] + noise * (Math.random() - 0.5) * 2));
        }
        r = rn; t += dt;
      }
    }
    yield {r, t};
  }
}
rnCanvas = mkCanvas(760, 400)
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
{
  const {r, t} = rnState, {ev, mmax, N} = rnKernel, c = rnCanvas, fg = exFg();
  const W = 760, H = 400; c.clearRect(0, 0, W, H); c.font = exFont;
  const aP = {x0: 90, y0: 12, w: W - 110, h: 170};
  const rmax = Math.max(1e-6, ...r);
  axisBox(c, aP.x0, aP.y0, aP.w, aP.h);
  c.fillStyle = "#1f77b4";
  for (let i = 0; i < N; i++) { const bh = aP.h * r[i] / rmax; c.fillRect(aP.x0 + aP.w * i / N, aP.y0 + aP.h - bh, aP.w / N, bh); }
  c.fillStyle = fg; c.textAlign = "right"; c.fillText("activity", aP.x0 - 8, aP.y0 + aP.h / 2 + 5);
  c.textAlign = "center"; c.fillText(`position on the ring · t = ${t.toFixed(0)} τ`, aP.x0 + aP.w / 2, aP.y0 + aP.h + 22);
  const sP = {x0: 90, y0: 240, w: W - 110, h: 110};
  const M = 40, emax = Math.max(1.6, ...ev), emin = Math.min(-0.5, ...ev);
  const sy = v => sP.y0 + sP.h * (1 - (v - emin) / (emax - emin));
  axisBox(c, sP.x0, sP.y0, sP.w, sP.h);
  c.setLineDash([4, 4]); c.strokeStyle = "red"; c.beginPath(); c.moveTo(sP.x0, sy(1)); c.lineTo(sP.x0 + sP.w, sy(1)); c.stroke(); c.setLineDash([]);
  c.strokeStyle = "#888"; c.beginPath(); c.moveTo(sP.x0, sy(0)); c.lineTo(sP.x0 + sP.w, sy(0)); c.stroke();
  for (let m = 0; m <= M; m++) { c.fillStyle = m === mmax ? "#ff7f0e" : "gray"; c.beginPath(); c.arc(sP.x0 + sP.w * m / M, sy(ev[m]), 4, 0, 2 * Math.PI); c.fill(); }
  c.fillStyle = fg; c.textAlign = "right"; c.fillText("eigenvalue", sP.x0 - 8, sP.y0 + sP.h / 2 + 5); c.fillText("1", sP.x0 - 8, sy(1) + 5); c.fillText("0", sP.x0 - 8, sy(0) + 5);
  c.textAlign = "center"; c.fillText(`spatial frequency (waves around the ring) · amplified most: ${mmax}`, sP.x0 + sP.w / 2, sP.y0 + sP.h + 22);
  c.fillText("0", sP.x0, sP.y0 + sP.h + 42); c.fillText(M, sP.x0 + sP.w, sP.y0 + sP.h + 42);
  return c.canvas;
}
```

**What you see.** Top: the activity $r$ of each neuron as a blue bar, by
position on the ring. Bottom: the eigenvalues of $W$ for each spatial
frequency, counted in waves around the ring, as grey dots. The orange dot is the
largest eigenvalue, the frequency the network amplifies most. The red dashed
line marks eigenvalue 1, the boundary between decay and growth.

Try: with the gain below 1 the pattern fades and only the random input remains.
Above 1, the frequency marked in orange takes over. Make the inhibition wider
and the stripes get broader. From the pattern-formation exercise in
*Theoretical Neuroscience*.

## Hebbian learning in the weight plane

One neuron receives two inputs with activities $u_1, u_2$ through weights
$w = (w_1, w_2)$. Averaged over many input patterns, learning is driven by the
input correlation matrix $Q = \langle u u^{\mathsf T} \rangle$, here
$Q = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & q \\ q & 1 \end{pmatrix}$, where $q$ is the
correlation between the two inputs (the slider). $\tau$ sets the learning
speed and $\alpha$ is the strength of the normalising term in Oja's rule.
Three rules:

$$\text{Hebbian:}\quad \tau \frac{dw}{dt} = Q\,w$$

$$\text{with bounds:}\quad \tau \frac{dw}{dt} = Q\,w, \qquad 0 \le w_i \le 1$$

$$\text{Oja:}\quad \tau \frac{dw}{dt} = Q\,w - \alpha\,(w^{\mathsf T} Q\, w)\,w$$

Pick a rule, then click anywhere in the weight plane to choose an initial
condition.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof hbRule = Inputs.radio(new Map([["Hebbian", "hebb"], ["Hebbian with bounds [0, 1]", "bounded"], ["Oja's rule", "oja"]]), {value: "hebb", label: "Rule"})
viewof hbQ = Inputs.range([-1, 1], {value: -0.4, step: 0.05, label: "Input correlation q"})
viewof hbAlpha = Inputs.range([0.2, 3], {value: 1, step: 0.1, label: "Oja α (Oja's rule only)"})
viewof hbPause = Inputs.toggle({label: "Pause"})
viewof hbReplay = Inputs.button("Replay")
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
hbCol = ({C0: "#1f77b4", C1: "#ff7f0e", C2: "#2ca02c", K: "#444", T1: "#9467bd", T2: "#17becf"})
hbLay = ({W: 760, H: 400, S: 340, m: 80, top: 16})   // plane occupies x in [m, m+S], y in [top, top+S]
mutable hbClick = null
hbCanvas = {
  const c = mkCanvas(hbLay.W, hbLay.H);
  c.canvas.style.cursor = "crosshair";
  c.canvas.addEventListener("click", ev => {
    const r = c.canvas.getBoundingClientRect();
    const x = (ev.clientX - r.left) * hbLay.W / r.width, y = (ev.clientY - r.top) * hbLay.H / r.height;
    const {m, S, top} = hbLay;
    if (x < m || x > m + S || y < top || y > top + S) return;
    mutable hbClick = {fx: (x - m) / S, fy: 1 - (y - top) / S};
  });
  return c;
}
hbLimits = ({hebb: [-2, 2], bounded: [-0.1, 1.1], oja: [-1.2, 1.2]})
hbStart = {
  const [lo, hi] = hbLimits[hbRule];
  if (!hbClick) return [0.01, 0.05];
  return [lo + (hi - lo) * hbClick.fx, lo + (hi - lo) * hbClick.fy];
}
hbStep = (w, rule, q, alpha, dt = 0.1) => {
  const Qw = [w[0] + q * w[1], q * w[0] + w[1]];
  let n;
  if (rule === "oja") { const wQw = w[0] * Qw[0] + w[1] * Qw[1];
    n = [w[0] + dt * (Qw[0] - alpha * wQw * w[0]), w[1] + dt * (Qw[1] - alpha * wQw * w[1])]; }
  else n = [w[0] + dt * Qw[0], w[1] + dt * Qw[1]];
  if (rule === "bounded") n = [Math.min(1, Math.max(0, n[0])), Math.min(1, Math.max(0, n[1]))];
  return n;
}
hbEndColour = (w, rule) => {
  const near = (a, b, tol) => Math.abs(w[0] - a) < tol && Math.abs(w[1] - b) < tol;
  if (rule === "bounded") { if (near(1, 1, 1e-3)) return hbCol.C0; if (near(0, 1, 1e-3)) return hbCol.C1; if (near(1, 0, 1e-3)) return hbCol.C2; }
  if (rule === "oja") { const r = Math.SQRT1_2; if (near(r, r, 0.02)) return hbCol.C0; if (near(-r, r, 0.02)) return hbCol.C1; if (near(r, -r, 0.02)) return hbCol.C2; }
  return hbCol.K;
}
hbField = {
  const N = 20, steps = 100, trajs = [];
  for (let i = 0; i < N; i++) for (let j = 0; j < N; j++) {
    let w = [i / (N - 1), j / (N - 1)]; const pts = [w];
    for (let s = 0; s < steps; s++) { w = hbStep(w, hbRule, hbQ, hbAlpha); pts.push(w); }
    trajs.push({pts, col: hbEndColour(w, hbRule)});
  }
  return trajs;
}
hbTraj = {
  hbReplay;
  const steps = 100; let w = hbStart; const pts = [w]; let k = 0;
  while (true) {
    if (!viewof hbPause.value && k < steps) { w = hbStep(w, hbRule, hbQ, hbAlpha); pts.push(w); k++; }
    yield {pts, done: k >= steps, col: k >= steps ? hbEndColour(w, hbRule) : hbCol.K};
  }
}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
{
  const c = hbCanvas, fg = exFg(), {W, H, S, m, top} = hbLay;
  const [lo, hi] = hbLimits[hbRule];
  const px = w => m + S * (w - lo) / (hi - lo), py = w => top + S * (1 - (w - lo) / (hi - lo));
  c.clearRect(0, 0, W, H); c.font = exFont;
  axisBox(c, m, top, S, S);
  c.fillStyle = fg; c.textAlign = "center";
  c.fillText("w₁", m + S / 2, top + S + 24); c.fillText(lo, px(lo), top + S + 24); c.fillText(hi, px(hi), top + S + 24);
  c.textAlign = "right"; c.fillText("w₂", m - 10, top + S / 2 + 5); c.fillText(lo, m - 8, py(lo) + 5); c.fillText(hi, m - 8, py(hi) + 5);
  c.save(); c.beginPath(); c.rect(m, top, S, S); c.clip();
  c.lineWidth = 1;
  for (const {pts, col} of hbField) {
    c.strokeStyle = col; c.globalAlpha = 0.25; c.beginPath();
    pts.forEach((p, i) => i ? c.lineTo(px(p[0]), py(p[1])) : c.moveTo(px(p[0]), py(p[1]))); c.stroke();
  }
  c.globalAlpha = 1; c.lineWidth = 2.5; c.strokeStyle = hbTraj.col; c.beginPath();
  hbTraj.pts.forEach((p, i) => i ? c.lineTo(px(p[0]), py(p[1])) : c.moveTo(px(p[0]), py(p[1]))); c.stroke();
  const last = hbTraj.pts[hbTraj.pts.length - 1], first = hbTraj.pts[0];
  c.fillStyle = hbTraj.col; c.beginPath(); c.arc(px(last[0]), py(last[1]), 6, 0, 2 * Math.PI); c.fill();
  c.strokeStyle = fg; c.lineWidth = 1.5; c.beginPath(); c.arc(px(first[0]), py(first[1]), 6, 0, 2 * Math.PI); c.stroke();
  c.restore();
  c.fillStyle = fg; c.textAlign = "left"; c.fillText(`start (${first[0].toFixed(2)}, ${first[1].toFixed(2)}) · click to move`, m + 8, top + 22);
  // time course, right
  const x0 = m + S + 70, tW = W - x0 - 16;
  const tx = i => x0 + tW * i / 100, ty = w => py(w);
  axisBox(c, x0, top, tW, S);
  c.fillStyle = fg; c.textAlign = "center"; c.fillText("time steps", x0 + tW / 2, top + S + 24);
  c.fillText("0", tx(0), top + S + 24); c.fillText("100", tx(100), top + S + 24);
  c.textAlign = "right"; c.fillText(lo, x0 - 8, py(lo) + 5); c.fillText(hi, x0 - 8, py(hi) + 5);
  c.save(); c.beginPath(); c.rect(x0, top, tW, S); c.clip();
  for (const [j, col] of [[0, hbCol.T1], [1, hbCol.T2]]) {
    c.strokeStyle = col; c.lineWidth = 2; c.beginPath();
    hbTraj.pts.forEach((p, i) => i ? c.lineTo(tx(i), ty(p[j])) : c.moveTo(tx(i), ty(p[j]))); c.stroke();
  }
  c.restore();
  c.textAlign = "left"; c.fillStyle = hbCol.T1; c.fillText("w₁", x0 + 8, top + 22); c.fillStyle = hbCol.T2; c.fillText("w₂", x0 + 44, top + 22);
  return c.canvas;
}
```

**What you see.** Left: the weight plane, $w_1$ against $w_2$. The faint lines
are trajectories from a grid of starting points, coloured by where they end
after 100 steps. With bounds: blue ends at $(1,1)$, orange at $(0,1)$, green at
$(1,0)$. With Oja's rule: blue ends at $(1,1)/\sqrt2$, orange at $(-1,1)/\sqrt2$,
green at $(1,-1)/\sqrt2$. Grey means none of these, which for plain Hebbian
learning is every trajectory, since they all run off to infinity. The thick
line is your trajectory, starting at the open circle and ending at the filled
dot, which takes the colour of its end state once it has arrived. Right: the
same trajectory as $w_1$ (purple) and $w_2$ (teal) against time.

Try: plain Hebbian learning runs away along the leading eigenvector of $Q$,
whichever way you start. With bounds the plane splits into basins of
attraction. Oja's rule keeps $|w|$ finite and converges to a normalised
eigenvector of $Q$. Change $q$ to see the basins move.
From the Hebbian learning exercise in *Theoretical Neuroscience*.
